paper_title: Selection Is Not Learning: Choosing Model Futures

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Self-evolving language models train on tasks they generate, so every round must decide which updated model the next round inherits. Current loops such as R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill Self-Play make this decision through the task, admitting tasks that look learnable and inheriting every resulting update. We identify a selection-to-update gap in these loops, where a task that looks learnable need not produce a useful update. Most updates on verified tasks fail to make correct answers more likely, yet these loops inherit them all. HeirCommit freezes the updated model and uses fresh evaluation questions to decide whether to inherit it or retain the current model. EvoHeir separates parameter inheritance from experience inheritance, using current and archived experience to repair failures and preserve successes before final confirmation. Our analysis characterizes selection-induced optimism and decomposes regret into selection, absorption, and confirmation errors. HeirCommit cuts the harmful share of accepted updates by 68-83% relative to random inheritance at the same acceptance rate. Across four backbones, EvoHeir achieves the best mathematics and general-reasoning averages, raising the math average by 5.3% relative to the strongest baseline, Agent0. The framework lets useful experience persist even when the model that produced it is not inherited.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Self-evolving language models generate tasks and train on their own outputs (Huang et al., 2026a; Xia et al., 2026; Huang et al., 2026b). Each inherited update changes both the learner and the curriculum of later rounds, allowing progress or regressions to accumulate (Shao et al., 2026). Self-training can even raise models target metric and then collapse it within the same training campaign (Lin, 2026). The central decision is therefore which learning outcomes to carry forward. Task-side selection leaves selection-to-update gap: pass rate, disagreement, and frontier proximity describe pre-training behavior, not the transfer produced by an optimizer update. In our audits, 4252% of native Agent0/R-Zero admissions leave the frontier under independent responses. Even with exact-valid tasks, 60 of 96 Skill Self-Play (Skill-SP) updates have nonpositive correct-target NLL gain. Learning opportunities must ultimately be judged by the states they produce. HEIRCOMMIT judges realized transitions: it freezes successor, compares it with the current model (the root) on fresh probes, and inherits that state or retains root. Fresh evidence separates confirmation from the noise that favored the proposal during selection. The deeper question is the granularity of inheritance. SOAR uses actual student improvement to reward teacher (Sundaram et al., 2026), and APE evaluates candidate fine-tunings before accepting updates (Marın, 2025). Pre-commit skill verification (Shang et al., 2026) and anytime-valid certificates (Sengupta, 2026) gate agent updates while the base model stays frozen. Whole-state acceptance nevertheless couples branchs gains and losses. Must useful experience donor also supply the next learners parameters? Separating these choices opens learning path beyond whole-state acceptance (Figure 1). EVOHEIR separates parameter inheritance from experience inheritance. Screening picks the recipient that supplies the next learners parameters, either branch endpoint or the current model. EXPERIENCE RECOVERY then repairs this recipients failures with current and archived reference solutions while preserving its successes. HEIRCOMMIT confirms the completed post-absorption state against root. Qualified experience enters the archive regardless of this decision: parameter inheritance can stop without discarding material that helps later recipient. We evaluate HEIRCOMMIT on the native updates of three self-evolution hosts, and EVOHEIR on four backbones over ten rounds. HEIRCOMMIT cuts the harmful share of accepted updates by 6883% relative to random inheritance at the same acceptance rate, on every host. EVOHEIR achieves the highest mathematics and general-reasoning averages on all four backbones and beats Agent0 on 45 of 48 benchmarkbackbone pairs. References from eight of ten donors weaker than the current model still improve the recipient. Our contributions are: 1. We identify the selection-to-update gap and prove that pre-update behavior alone cannot identify an updates value. Reusing screening evidence to accept branch pays union bound over branches, which fresh confirmation removes. 2. We introduce HEIRCOMMIT, source-independent rule that commits frozen successor only when it beats the current model on fresh probes. On the native updates of R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill-SP, it turns negative pool gain positive on two of the three hosts. 3. We develop EVOHEIR, which decides separately which parameters the next learner inherits and which experience it absorbs. Across four backbones it raises the base models math average by 7.930.1%, the most of any compared method. 4. We show that experience outlives the model that produced it. Recovery beats direct fine-tuning on the same 64 references by 1.93 pp on average, and experience from rounds whose model was rejected adds 0.66 pp beyond committed-round history.

sections.content: We first test whether task selection predicts learning and whether HEIRCOMMIT repairs inheritance, then evaluate the complete loop on four backbones, and finally measure the value of experience, each component, and the cost of construction. 6.1 TASK SELECTION DOES NOT PREDICT LEARNING Reusing responses both to select target and to score it inflates the targets support. Selected-target optimism, the drop from candidates score on its selection responses to its score on fresh responses, is 8.60 pp in Agent0 and 4.10 pp in R-Zero, as Figure 4a shows, while fixed-target controls stay near zero at 0.20 and 0.10 pp. Under fresh responses, 52.2% of Agent0s and 42.0% of R-Zeros admitted tasks also leave the native frontier. Even exact-valid tasks need not teach. sections.title: 7 CONCLUSION
sections.content: We identify the selection-to-update gap: admitting task that looks learnable does not ensure useful update, and 60 of 96 updates on verified tasks show no gain. HEIRCOMMIT inherits successor only when it beats the current model on fresh probes and cuts the harmful share of commits by 6883% on three self-evolution hosts. EVOHEIR separates the parameters round inherits from the experience it keeps and raises the math average by up to 7.0% over Agent0, the strongest baseline. Self-evolving systems should judge the updates they produce, not only the tasks they choose, and keep experience beyond the models that produced it.

sections.title: IMPLEMENTATION CONFIGURATION
sections.content: Appendix and Table 3 give the EVOHEIR (Full) recipe. The remaining implementation details are as follows. Response-token aggregation. Response loss is computed only on recorded response tokens; prompt tokens are masked out. If an EOS token is present in the recorded response, it is included in the loss. Truncated responses contribute their available response prefix without synthesizing missing EOS token. Token-level forward KL over the full vocabulary is averaged within each response, then over questions, so repair and keep examples have equal per-question weight. Absorption and optimizer state. Recovery uses AdamW with learning rate 5 105, (β1, β2) = (0.9, 0.999), epsilon 108, zero weight decay, gradient clipping at 1.0, and LoRA dropout 0. The adapter has rank 8, scaling α = 16, and targets proj and proj; absorption uses at most 16 updates. After absorption, the adapter is merged into the recipient and the merged weights are reloaded and checked for exact consistency. If the absorbed model is accepted, it becomes the next native root and the native optimizer and scheduler are reinitialized; Recovery optimizer state is not carried into native training. If the proposal is rejected, the original root is retained with its parameters, optimizer moments, scheduler, and random state unchanged. At the next rounds native-stage boundary, the native optimizer and scheduler are reinitialized for whichever model was inherited. Rollback restores the root snapshot; it does not carry Recovery moments into later stage. Archive policy. The archive stores at most 256 qualified training records, deduplicated by normalized problem identity. Conflicting labels, verification conflicts, known reasoning errors, incomplete responses, and non-training records are excluded. When capacity is exceeded, records are selected deterministically using round/source-stratified round-robin admission, with stable hash ordering within each group. Recovery budget. Each round nominates up to 32 exploration records and 32 learner-success records, and recipient attempts reuse exact-checkpoint cached responses or use one additional response within 64generation budget. Recovery makes single pass with at most 16 optimizer updates, capped at 131,072 response loss tokens and 262,144 combined teacher and student forward tokens. An empty usable pool leaves Ssel unchanged.
